svg.text: updateScore() downcasts with instanceof — it is NOT
on the interface, so a mock impl silently no-ops.
ids in, ids out — no entity ever crosses as an argument ✓
updateScore is MISSING from the interface — the biggest
gap in this design, and the reason the facade downcasts.
getMatch returns the LIVE Match, not a DTO — callers can
reach in and call start()/end() straight past the guards.
THE CORE — three registries + the guards
ids are UUID.randomUUID().toString() — no natural keys
createTeam / addPlayer / scheduleMatch — lookup, build, register
updateScore — requires status == IN_PROGRESS (NOT on the iface)
endMatch — requires IN_PROGRESS + a resolvable winner
getMatch / getAllMatches — snapshot copy of values()
every mutator does lookup-or-throw FIRST, then status-or-throw ✓
missing entity ⇒ IllegalArgument; wrong phase ⇒ IllegalState ✓
CHM gives per-KEY atomicity only. The status check and the
mutation that follows are NOT atomic together — two threads
can both pass "status == IN_PROGRESS" and both end the match.
Fix: synchronize on the Match, or make status a CAS field.
System.out.println sits inside every mutator — domain code doing
presentation. Fine for a demo, the first thing to strip in review.
No listener registry: "live updates" are those printlns today.
THE AGGREGATES — Match owns the lifecycle
id, team1, team2, venue, startTime — all final
status: MatchStatus · winner: Team (null until COMPLETED)
setScore(team, score) — ABSOLUTE set, matched by reference identity
end() updates both teams' W/L in one call — no way to record half of it ✓
setScore takes a TOTAL, not a delta — so no run is ever "added"; a caller
that passes a stale total silently rewrites history. And a third team is a no-op.
id, name, country (final) · wins, losses: int
an if with no else. Should throw.
these three mutators are NEVER CALLED by the service.
Player stats stay at zero forever — dead accumulators.
MODELLED BUT NOT WIRED — be upfront about this
Nothing constructs a Ball. Match has no List<Ball>.
Ball-by-ball scoring is DESIGNED, not IMPLEMENTED.
It is the right shape though — see the sticky on the right.
• No Innings, no Over, no Scorecard class
• No Observer registry — no subscribe/notify anywhere
• No toss, no target, no overs limit, no DLS
• No draw / tie — end() demands a winning Team
Listing your own gaps is what separates "I shipped a
skeleton and I know it" from "I think this is complete". ✓

g.text: recordBall(matchId, ball) replaces updateScore as the
only write path. One append, three derived effects:
• score becomes a SUM over balls, not a settable int
Event log first, aggregates derived. Then a mis-recorded
ball is fixable by editing one event, not the total.
"LIVE UPDATES" — WHAT OBSERVER WOULD ACTUALLY COST
Today a score change prints to stdout. To make it real you need
three things, and none of them are large:
dominate, writes are rare, so COW beats a lock
3. notify AFTER the mutation, OUTSIDE the lock — never call a
stranger's code while holding your own monitor
Point 3 is what gets probed: a slow listener must never stall the scorer.

svg.text: ① Cricinfo facade → CricinfoService seam → ② CricinfoServiceImpl: three CHM registries + lookup-then-status guards → ③ Match aggregate (Team, Player) → ④ name what is stubbed: Ball, Observer, innings

g.text: Patterns: Facade · enum state machine · registry-of-aggregates · Observer (not yet built)
Cricket live scores — teams, squads, match lifecycle — LLD skeleton
